added.title: Software Engineering Intern
added.description:
As a Software Engineering Intern at AoPS, you will play a supportive role in our mission to innovate and enhance educational technologies. In this role, you will assist with the development of software programs and gain hands-on experience in a collaborative environment focused on problem-solving and technological advancement.

The Software Engineering Intern Will

Develops, tests, and implements new software programs under the guidance of experienced software engineers.
Participates in code reviews, learning to evaluate and improve program quality.
Supports the maintenance and improvement of existing programs.
Documents new and existing programs in various formats, focusing on clarity and usability.
Engages with Engineering Leadership and team members to learn and apply best development practices.
Collaborates on product development strategy and specifications with Product Owners, Project Managers, and Designers.
Communicates effectively about development tasks and timelines and understands project management basics.
Engages in both individual and collaborative development efforts.
Completes other tasks and responsibilities, as assigned.

The Ideal Candidate Has

Currently pursuing an undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field
Excellent problem-solving, analytical, and creative skills
Knowledge of programming and debugging fundamentals in at least one language
Strong technical and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to give and receive constructive feedback
Web development experience with JavaScript, React, PHP, Node.js, MySQL, or PostgreSQL is not required, but nice to have

Why Join AoPS

This is a 40-hour per week paid internship with a pay rate of $30/hour. The internship will take place in summer 2027 and will be based at our headquarters in San Diego, CA. Most of our interns are with us for 10 - 12 weeks, starting in late May or early June. Here are some things you can look forward to:

Impact: Gain hands-on experience in Software Engineering and play a supportive role in our mission to innovate and enhance educational technologies.
Flexibility: Casual work environment with a hybrid work week and flexible scheduling
Future Planning: 401(k) with company match
Quality of Life: Paid Sick Leave
Ease of Transition: Relocation bonus (if currently located outside of San Diego)

Background Check

Please note that employment is contingent on the successful completion of a background check.

Work Authorization

Please note that in order to be considered for this position you must be legally authorized to work in the US. We are unable to offer sponsorship, including STEM-OPT and H-1B.

About AoPS

Art of Problem Solving (AoPS) is on a mission to discover, inspire, and train the great problem solvers of the next generation. Since 2003, we have trained hundreds of thousands of the country’s top students, including nearly all the members of the US International Math Olympiad team, through our online school, in-person academies, textbooks, and online learning systems. While our primary focus has been math for most of our history, through the years we have expanded our unique problem solving curriculum into more subjects, such as language arts, science, and computer science.

added.title: Software Test Engineer I
added.description:
Werfen is a growing, family-owned, innovative company founded in 1966 in Barcelona, Spain. We are a worldwide leader in specialized diagnostics in the areas of Hemostasis, Acute Care Diagnostics, Transfusion, Autoimmunity, and Transplant. Through our Original Equipment Manufacturing (OEM) business line, we research, develop, and manufacture customized assays and biomaterials. We operate directly in 30 countries, and in more than 100 territories through distributors. Our Headquarters and Technology Centers are located in the US and Europe, and our workforce is more than 7,000 strong.

Our success comes from a specific focus in these rapidly evolving diagnostic areas, our commitment to customers, and our dedication to innovation and quality. We’re passionate about providing healthcare professionals the most valuable and complete solutions to improve hospital efficiency and enhance patient care.

Overview

Job Summary

Participate in software development for medical device applications by independently implementing and testing well defined software features features, developing automated tests, and improving code quality. Contribute throughout the software development life cycle, including design, construction, debugging, and testing. Ensure reliable, compliant software by applying engineering and quality practices with increasing autonomy. This role adds value by advancing product quality, accelerating development velocity, and elevating coding and testing standards within the team. The position’s unique contribution is delivering quality features and test assets that strengthen overall system reliability.

Responsibilities

Key Accountabilities

Design and implement well defined software features and/or manual/automated test cases and frameworks within established architectural guidelines. Success measured through working, maintainable implementations; adherence to coding and quality standards; and well-reasoned design improvements.
Drive technical excellence by following and reinforcing development and testing standards, participating actively in code reviews, and improving documentation quality. Success measured through strong review contributions, and improved documentation.
Contribute to design discussions, architectural evaluations, and code reviews, influencing decisions with thoughtful technical input. Success measured through quality of technical contributions and demonstrated ability to articulate and defend technical choices.
Seeking guidance from senior engineers when needed. Success measured through measurable skill growth, positive feedback, and ability to explain technical concepts effectively.
Champion software quality by developing manual and/or automated test cases/frameworks, and maintaining documentation standards. Success measured through improved test coverage metrics, reduced defect rates, enhanced documentation quality, and successful adoption of automated testing approaches.
Proactively identify and implement process improvements within the team's workflow. Success requires successful implementation of process improvements, measurable efficiency gains in team workflows, and positive adoption by team members.
Performs other duties and responsibilities as assigned Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

Networking/Key relationships

Development and Testing Teams - Take a role in daily development and testing activities. Ensure software meets requirements, adheres to standards, and is properly tested throughout the development lifecycle. Contribute to technical discussions and decision-making processes.
Technical Lead/Senior Engineers - Maintain regular collaboration on technical design and implementation strategies. Seek guidance on complex technical challenges and architectural decisions while participating in estimation activities. Focus on developing technical expertise through mentorship from senior team members.
Any other based on departmental or project needs

Qualifications

Minimum Knowledge & Experience required for the position:

Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related technical field

Experience: 0-3 years of professional software development experience

Management has the discretion of substituting relevant work experience for a degree and/or making exceptions to the years of experience requirement.

Skills & Capabilities

Proficiency in multiple programming languages, with the ability to learn additional languages as needed.
Understanding of software architecture principles, design patterns, and their practical implementation.
Knowledge of Agile software development practices.
Understanding of database technologies and data structures.
Knowledge of version control systems and collaborative development tools.
Understanding of software security principles and best practices.
Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly.

Travel Requirements

This position requires minimal travel. Expect to travel approximately 5% annually. These trips will be for attending important team meetings/events where physical presence is beneficial for collaborative work sessions, strategic planning, or team-building purposes. Occasional additional travel may be required.

Closing

If you are interested in constantly learning and being challenged on a daily basis we encourage you to submit your resume or CV.

added.title: Software Engineer (Portal)
added.description:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array and parabolic ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role:

Northwood is looking for a Software Engineer focusing on control systems for our Phased Array antennas. As a Software Engineer at Northwood, you will be pivotal in designing, implementing, and optimizing the global service that delivers connectivity to our customers. You will have ownership over key areas ranging from control of our antenna systems to high-rate data processing. An ideal candidate is someone who likes to work across areas of responsibility and can dive deep into high-priority challenges.

We seek versatile candidates who want to contribute across multiple areas while having a solid foundation in a few core areas of focus
. These areas of focus include (but are not limited to) the following:

Algorithms for antenna calibration and localization
Algorithms for beamforming and antenna pointing
Digital signal processing on high-rate data streams
Telecommunications systems
Multi-antenna orchestration
Fault detection, isolation, and recovery (FDIR) systems
API, Database, and Inter-Process Communication (IPC) design
Software simulations for test and verification

Basic Qualifications:

3+ years of professional software development experience. This doesn’t have to be a full-time role. There are many ways to gain valuable experience, and we’d love to hear about yours; please tell us about internships, projects out of the classroom, or any personal wo.
A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Math, Physics, or other related discipline. This is a soft-requirement; if you didn’t pursue a degree, tell us why and what you've done in its place.

Preferred Qualifications:

While we don’t expect you to have every skill listed below, we do expect you to take ownership of one or more areas and drive decisions and implementations where your strengths lie.

Programming Languages (General): Rust, C, C++, Go, Python, Java
Strong problem-solving abilities
Excellent communication and collaboration skills
Ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment
High mathematical maturity

Domain specific skills:

APIs and Inter-Service Communication:
Experience in building RESTful APIs
Experience with Protocol Buffers and/or gRPC
Antenna Systems
Knowledge of the physics of Phased Arrays and beamforming
Familiarity with spatial filtering and adaptive beamforming methods
Data Movement and Networking:
Proficiency in architecting data pipelines for high-throughput environments
Understanding of network programming and IP protocols
Experience with high-speed communications (10/25/100G Ethernet)
Databases and Data Processing:
Proficiency with relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL)
Knowledge of publish/subscribe architectures and technologies (RabbitMQ, MQTT, Redis Pub/Sub, etc.)
Distributed Systems and Cloud Computing:
Experience designing and implementing distributed systems
Knowledge of cloud services (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) and orchestration tools
Familiarity with microservice architectures
Hardware Interaction and FPGAs:
Experience with hardware control systems
Familiarity with FPGA programming and orchestration
Understanding of embedded systems development
Parallel Systems
Experience writing multithreaded systems
Knowledge of synchronization primitives, including mutexes, semaphores, and message passing queues
Experience with asynchronous programming
Signal Processing
Knowledge of signal processing mathematics, particularly digital signal processing (e.g., Discrete Fourier Transforms, Filtering, Quantization, etc.)
Experience implementing signal processing routines on real systems
Simulation
Experience designing/implementing simulations for physical models (think satellite orbits) or hardware systems
Telecommunications:
Knowledge of modulation schemes and modems
Knowledge of error correction and coding schemes, including linear block codes, convolutional codes, and Reed-Solomon codes
Testing and Automation:
Experience with automated testing frameworks
Familiarity with production line testing software

Additional Information:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know at accommodations@northwoodspace.io

added.title: Analytics Data Engineer
added.description:
Agency

Carmichael Lynch

Job Function

Data and Analytics

Job Subfunction

Data Engineering

Role

Job Description:

As a data engineer, you’ll work across a dynamic client roster designing and building data solutions that connect media, site, and marketing performance data into actionable insights. You will partner closely with analytics, strategy, media, and client teams to architect scalable data solutions that answer business questions and support marketing decision-making.

This role requires a hands-on, solution-oriented engineer who combines deep technical expertise with a strong understanding of media and digital analytics. The ideal candidate proactively identifies opportunities, solves complex data challenges, and helps shape how data is leveraged across the agency and our clients.

What You’ll Do

Design data solutions that solve client business needs

Partner with analytics and media teams to understand business objectives and translate them into scalable data solutions.
Design data models that integrate media, site, sales and media conversion data to provide a complete view of marketing performance.
Recommend and implement measurement approaches that support both agency and client objectives.
Serve as a subject matter expert on media and marketing data architecture.

Lead media data engineering initiatives

Build and maintain integrations across major advertising, analytics, and marketing technology platforms.
Develop scalable frameworks for campaign performance measurement, attribution, audience analysis, and optimization.
Evaluate emerging platforms, APIs, and data sources to improve agency capabilities and client outcomes.

Build and maintain data pipelines

Automate data pipelines with speed, accuracy, and scalability in mind.
Own day-to-day health of data pipelines: scheduling, monitoring, alerting and failure recovery
Apply DataOps best practices maintaining high stands of quality and security across each stage of development
Write and optimize SQL views, Python/R scripts, and API connectors as needed.
Continually optimize data cleaning and anomaly detection processes.
Help manage and advance our GCP infrastructure, particularly with BigQuery and GCP integrations.

Own data quality and governance

Maintain rigorous QA practices to ensure clean, reliable, and consistent data.
Continuously seek opportunities to improve processes and infrastructure.

Problem solves relentlessly

Proactively catch and investigate issues, finding root causes and going beyond surface solutions.
Work with analysts to anticipate needs and ensure data is easy to find and use.
Demonstrate situational awareness, knowing when to escalate, push or pull back, or execute.
Communicate effectively with less technical stakeholders to address challenges and keep them updated on progress.

You Could Be a Good Fit If

You take ownership of data quality and availability like it’s mission critical.
You already are, or have the drive to become, an expert in media data.
You’re a problem solver who doesn’t stop at “it’s broken.” You figure out why and how to fix it.
You balance speed and accuracy, knowing both matter in a client-driven environment.
You’re adaptable, resourceful, and curious. You’re able to figure things out with limited direction. Learning new things and finding creative solutions are some of your favorite parts of your job.

Requirements

Education:

A bachelor’s degree preferred or equivalent work experience in related field such as Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics/Statistics, Marketing Analytics, etc.

Skills And Experience

2-4 years of experience in data engineering, marketing analytics, media analytics, or related disciplines. Agency experience strongly preferred.
Expert-level SQL and Python skills with experience developing scalable production-grade data pipelines.
Deep experience working with digital media data, including campaign delivery, audience, conversion, and attribution datasets.
Proven experience designing and implementing data solutions that support media planning, optimization, measurement, and reporting.
Strong understanding of digital marketing ecosystems including platforms such as Google Ads, CM360, DV360, The Trade Desk, Meta, LinkedIn, Adobe Analytics, and Google Analytics 4.
Experience integrating multiple data sources including media, site analytics, offline conversion, and first-party customer data.
Deep experience with BigQuery, GCP, or similar cloud-based data warehouse environments.
Experience evaluating client business requirements and translating them into scalable technical solutions.
Experience building data products, automated reporting frameworks, and measurement solutions for internal and external stakeholders.

Competencies (characteristics and work style)

Understands both the technical and business implications of data solutions.
Able to recommend approaches rather than simply execute requirements.
Builds credibility with clients and internal stakeholders through expertise and thoughtful problem solving.
Demonstrates ownership, initiative, and accountability from project inception through delivery.
Comfortable influencing decisions and challenging assumptions when a better solution exists.

The Electro Optical Infrared Systems (EOIS) line of business within DRS has locations in Dallas and Austin, TX, Melbourne, FL, and Cypress, CA. We offer an exciting and challenging work environment, a competitive salary and benefits package, and a business culture that rewards performance.

Employing the world’s brightest. Supporting the world’s bravest.

As a software engineer you will be working within a team that develops, tests and maintains a suite of data collection, processing, storage and viewing tools supporting the development and testing of infrared sensors and systems. You will have exposure to cutting edge languages and frameworks within a business leading the innovation in the infrared space.

Responsible for software engineering tasks including requirements/user story definition, software application and library design, implementation, integration, verification, validation and maintenance.
Responsible for adhering to the DRS engineering processes.
Other duties as assigned.

B.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering or a related discipline from an accredited institution.
0+ years of experience in full stack web development/software engineering

Excellent written and verbal communication skills

JavaScript
Python
Go
GRPC
Microservices

Familiarity with source control systems such as git
College level mathematics (calculus, statistics, linear algebra, etc.)

added.title: Software Engineer III – Release Engineering
added.description:
Business Unit

Cubic Defense

Company Details

We are seeking a junior-to-mid-level software engineer to own and improve the release process for a distributed software platform, coordinating its releases with the broader product release cycle.

The platform comprises a web-based control plane, runtime services, platform adapters, deployment charts, supporting components, and shared contract libraries. This engineer will work across those components to assemble, validate, document, and deliver reliable releases.

This role is well suited to an engineer who enjoys automation, systems integration, and making complex release processes predictable. The successful candidate will initially execute releases with support from senior engineers and progressively assume end-to-end ownership.

Job Details

We are seeking an experienced, self-directed software engineer to own and improve the release process for a distributed software platform, coordinating its releases with the broader product release cycle.

The platform comprises a web-based control plane, runtime services, platform adapters, deployment charts, supporting components, and shared contract libraries. This engineer will work independently across those components to assemble, validate, document, and deliver reliable releases, exercising sound technical judgment and coordinating with component owners as needed.

This role is well suited to a self-starter who enjoys automation, systems integration, and making complex release processes predictable. The successful candidate will assume end-to-end release ownership, proactively resolve issues, and provide technical coverage for senior engineers within the release-engineering scope when needed.

Key Responsibilities

Independently investigate and fix software defects and update dependencies to address security vulnerabilities, assessing the impact on release stability.
Own the planning and execution of platform releases in coordination with the broader product release schedule.
Coordinate versioning and release readiness across repositories, services, deployment charts, container images, and supporting components, proactively resolving dependency and readiness gaps.
Own and maintain release branches, tags, changelogs, release notes, and supporting documentation to ensure consistency and traceability.
Design, build, and improve CI/CD automation for compiling, testing, packaging, publishing, and deploying releases.
Plan and execute release validation in representative environments before promotion, evaluating results and addressing readiness concerns.
Verify compatibility among control-plane services, runtime components, platform adapters, shared contracts, and supported integrations, identifying and coordinating resolution of cross-component issues.
Track and assess dependencies and component revisions included in each release, identifying changes that create compatibility or delivery risk.
Coordinate with engineers, product owners, quality teams, platform teams, and other stakeholders to align release scope, timing, and readiness, resolving issues within the role’s scope and escalating broader decisions.
Independently investigate failed builds, deployments, and release-validation tests, identify root causes, and drive corrective action with the appropriate component owners.
Develop and maintain documentation for known issues, upgrade requirements, rollback procedures, and operational considerations, using release findings to improve guidance.
Establish and improve repeatable release checklists, quality gates, and readiness reporting, applying technical judgment to identify risks and recommend release actions.
Proactively identify manual release steps, prioritize improvements, and incrementally replace them with safe, maintainable automation.
Own post-release verification and independently resolve or appropriately escalate release-related issues, providing release-engineering coverage for senior teammates when needed.

Required Qualifications

A minimum of 4 years of professional software engineering, DevOps, platform engineering, or release engineering experience.
Ability to obtain a security clearance
Strong working knowledge of Git, branching, tagging, pull requests, and structured versioning.
Hands-on experience building, maintaining, and troubleshooting CI/CD systems and automated build or deployment pipelines.
Working knowledge of containers and modern deployment environments.
Ability to independently read, troubleshoot, and make changes to code in at least one modern programming language.
Experience working independently across multiple repositories and assessing dependencies between components.
Experience diagnosing complex build, test, configuration, or deployment failures and driving issues through resolution.
Strong written communication, attention to detail, and ability to clearly communicate technical risks and recommended actions.
Ability to independently own an established release process, exercise sound judgment, and implement practical improvements.
Ability to proactively coordinate work across multiple engineering teams and release schedules, following through on dependencies and commitments.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Kubernetes, deployment charts, container registries, and image promotion.
Familiarity with backend, frontend, or systems programming languages and frameworks.
Experience maintaining release notes, upgrade documentation, or deployment runbooks.
Familiarity with API contracts, service interfaces, and distributed systems.
Experience with integration or end-to-end testing in containerized environments.
Exposure to software supply-chain practices such as dependency scanning, artifact signing, SBOM generation, or vulnerability management.
Experience taking ownership of coordinated releases across related products or platforms.

added.description:
Wanna join the adventure?

Loft Orbital is looking for a Backend Software Engineer
to join the Mission Platform organization.

You'll work on a small and driven team, developing a brand new software product that optimizes tasking across a large heterogeneous constellation of multi-sensor satellites:

scale to fly 50+ satellites, serving 100,000s of customer tasking orders
design, build and optimize a brand new product from scratch
solve challenging problems across multiple domains:
Astrodynamics, satellite capacity modeling and simulation
Back-end/API performance
Low latency, high responsiveness system design
Mathematical optimization and scheduling problems

We're looking for someone with a solid background in software engineering, ideally with a proven track record of building systems from scratch and solving complex, system-level problems. The ideal candidate can operate independently in a fast-paced environment and challenge requirements.

About this role:

Develop and improve a new software product that manages customer orders across a multi-sensor constellation of satellites
Interface with teams to help design the customer-facing interfaces and the back-end pipeline that goes from a plan to onboard execution
Build tools and services that help sales and operators understand current and future capacity, operational risks and opportunities for growth
Solve complex multi-objective optimization problems that maximize collection capacity, balancing various (conflicting) customer constraints, and help define what “optimal” means
Design systems of systems: decompose complex problems into well-bounded services with clear interfaces, and reason about how they interact, fail, and scale together

Must Haves:

Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering, Physics/Astrodynamics, Mathematics or a related field
2+ years of experience with designing and developing software libraries and backend services, preferably in Python
Proven track record of operating independently and solving complex problems
Experience with system design
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, for technical and non-technical audiences

Nice to Haves:

Master’s degree in Software Engineering, Physics/Astrodynamics, Mathematics or a related field
5+ years of experience designing and developing software libraries and backend services, preferably in Python
Proficiency with Django/GraphQL stacks
Hands-on experience operating spacecraft
Experience with C++ / high-performance Python (vectorization, JIT compilation like Numba, GPU parallelization)
Demonstrated practical experience building high-performance backend software applications and/or libraries
Specialization in one of the following disciplines:
Integer/linear/multi-objective optimization or other Operations Research style problems
Back-end/API performance optimization
Distributed systems
Security
Earth observation tasking
High-performance computing

Some of Our Awesome Benefits:

100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents
Flexible Spending (FSA) and Health Savings (HSA) Accounts offered with an employer contribution to the HSA
100% employer paid Life, AD&D, Short-Term, and Long-Term Disability insurance
Flexible Time Off policy for vacation and sick leave, and 12 paid holidays
401(k) plan and equity options
Daily catered lunches and snacks
International exposure to our team in France
Fully paid parental leave; 14 weeks for primary caregiver and 10 weeks for secondary caregiver
Carrot Fertility provides comprehensive, inclusive fertility healthcare and family-forming benefits with financial support
Off-sites and many social events and celebrations
Relocation assistance when applicable

Who We Are

Loft: Space Made Simple.

Founded in 2017, Loft provides governments, companies, and research institutions with a fast, reliable, and simple way to deploy missions in orbit.

We integrate, launch, and operate spacecraft, offering end-to-end missions as a service across Earth observation, IoT connectivity, on-orbit AI, national security missions, and more. Leveraging our existing space infrastructure and an extensive inventory of satellite buses, Loft is reducing years-long integration and launch timelines to months. With more than 30 missions flown, Loft’s flight heritage and proven technologies enable customers to focus on their mission objectives.

With a growing fleet on track to reach 30 satellites by 2027, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, CA | Golden, CO | and Toulouse, France to meet accelerating demand for space infrastructure.

added.title: Software Engineer II, AWS DynamoDB
added.description:
Description

Want to help shape the future of one of the largest NoSQL database services on the planet?

The Amazon DynamoDB team is looking for deeply technical, team-first-mentality software engineers who are willing to commit themselves to providing best in class database performance to AWS customers.

DynamoDB is a key-value and document database that delivers single-digit-millisecond performance at any scale. As a fast-growing service at the core of the AWS Cloud, our business and engineering decisions have widespread impact across AWS, Amazon, and beyond. Many of the world's fastest growing businesses, such as Lyft, Airbnb, and Redfin, as well as enterprises, such as Samsung, Toyota, and Capital One, depend on the scale and performance of DynamoDB to support their mission-critical workloads.

DynamoDB engineers are constantly challenged to think of unique and innovative solutions. The quality bar is high. As an engineer here, you will work on the hardest engineering problems in distributed systems at a massive scale and on multiple dimensions. You will exercise your intellectual curiosity, work with motivated teams of sharp individuals, and get insightful guidance from senior and principal engineers.

Key job responsibilities

This is a hands-on position in which you will own everything from end to end: requirements gathering, designs, design reviews, implementations, code reviews, incremental feature launches, operations, mentoring, and the driving of continuous improvement.

A day in the life

As an Software Development Engineer on DynamoDB Storage, you'll own features end-to-end in the storage engine powering every DynamoDB read and write globally. Your days involve implementing changes in Java/Rust -- optimizing replication, reducing tail latency, or building new capabilities -- then validating through capacity tests across dozens of instance types. On on call (~1 week/quarter), you'll diagnose production issues across 30+ regions in real-time. You'll review teammates' code daily, contribute to designs spanning millions of nodes, and ship through rigorous phased rollouts. The work is deeply technical, exabyte-scale, and directly impacts DynamoDB's durability guarantees.

About The Team

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS? Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

Position Type

Full-Time/Regular

This is a remote-local position. Candidates should reside within commuting distance of Boston University and be available to come to campus as needed.

A cover letter is required for consideration.

Help secure a major research university's IT systems, and automate as much of that work as you can.

You'll work with technologists and business units across Boston University to define, implement, and evaluate security risks and controls, and to make sure what we build matches our enterprise architecture standards and Information Security policy.

You'll deploy and maintain security services, both commercial and home-grown, and help refine the policies and standards that govern them.

What makes this role different is how we expect the work to be done.

Security delivered as code, with version control, automated tests, and pipelines — and automated security checks living inside the pipelines our IS&T colleagues already use.

We also want real fluency with current AI tooling: working in AI-assisted development environments day to day, using AI to help generate and validate tests and review code, building AI-assisted security tooling and MCP integrations, and being the engineer who can look hard at the AI systems other units want to deploy and say something useful about them.

Raising everyone else's capability is a permanent part of this job, not a side project.

You'll pair with colleagues, build patterns they reuse, run working sessions, and be the person others come to with a question about doing this safely — and you'll keep doing it, because the tooling keeps moving.

Collaborative team, real problems, and strong benefits including tuition remission.

Required Skills

Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent experience; master's degree preferred.
3+ years of related experience in security engineering, security architecture, or adjacent infrastructure and software engineering roles.
Proficiency in at least one general-purpose programming language: Python, Go, Java, C#, or PowerShell.
Git-based version control, and experience building CI/CD pipelines that include automated testing.
Practical experience writing automated tests, including unit, integration, and regression tests.
Working knowledge of cloud and on-premises security controls, identity protocols, and network and system administration.
Demonstrated fluency with current AI tooling, including routine use of AI-assisted development environments and practical experience integrating large language models or AI services into working tools using tool and function calling, retrieval-augmented generation, or agentic patterns.
Judgment about where AI output requires verification, and an understanding of how AI-generated code and tests fail.
Working understanding of AI-specific security risk, including prompt injection, data leakage through model context, and authorization for agentic systems.
A track record of teaching or enabling colleagues: pairing, internal training, documentation others actually use, or reusable patterns adopted by a team.
Detail-oriented, with strong written and verbal communication skills.

If you do not meet these, you are still encouraged to apply; we value employees with a willingness to learn.
Model Context Protocol (MCP) server or client development.

DevSecOps tooling for dependency, container, secrets, and infrastructure-as-code scanning.
Higher education experience.

About Verily Health Inc.

At the intersection of technology, data science, and healthcare, Verily Health transforms complex health data into trusted intelligence, enabling health solutions that are more personal, predictive, and precise.

Verily’s flagship Governed Health Intelligence platform, Verily Pre, enables healthcare organizations to responsibly govern, model, and securely activate their protected health data at scale, deploying intelligence with the scientific rigor, oversight, and auditability needed for healthcare.

Description

As a Software Engineer at Verily, you will play a pivotal role in developing and enhancing products that are focused on the promise of precision health.

Verily Pre is a comprehensive, patient-centered platform that accelerates evidence generation for safer, more effective treatments and care decisions. Our cloud-first architecture, advanced analytics, and AI capabilities enable the collection, enrichment, and activation of petabytes of data, tailored to meet the unique needs of our partners. Pre’s Workbench solution provides a secure collaborative environment for data generators, research, and biopharma organizations to govern and analyze their data. Our software powers our customers in genomics research workflows, containerized AI development, and more.

The Platform Agents team is focused on delivering end-to-end agentic experiences to our Pre platform and Workbench solution users to empower and enable them to move quickly and safely in their healthcare and research work. Platform Agents drives an end to end experience, from the UI to harness to tools and model serving, alongside our other platform and AI squads.

Responsibilities

Work closely with the development team to design, develop, and deliver new full-stack agentic features across Verily Workbench and Pre Platform solutions.
Collaborate cross-functionally to identify dependencies, coordinate delivery, communicate design decisions and define requirements.
Come up with ideas to technical design problems, compare options, and propose solutions.
Develop using industry-standard tools including Google Cloud, Langgraph, Go, React, Terraform, and Kubernetes.

BA/BS degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent practical experience in software development.
5+ years of experience as a software developer in an industry setting.
2+ years experience building ML or LLM-powered software.
Experience with one or more general purpose programming languages including but not limited to: Java, C/C++, C#, Go, or Python.

Demonstrated experience in LLMOps and designing and implementing cloud software built on AI frameworks like Pytorch, Langgraph/Langchain, Google ADK, etc.
Experience building governance, observability, or auditability features into agentic systems.

Background working in ad-tech companies (e.g., Google Ads, Meta, Amazon Ads) or high-growth digital marketing agencies.

added.title: Software Engineer, Worldwide Amazon Stores Finance Technology, Controllership Engineering
added.description:
Description

Amazon's finance teams rely on financial controls to keep spending accurate and financial reports audit-ready. You will build the systems that automate those controls, catch errors and waste before money is spent, and give finance analysts fast, trusted answers through AI tools built on cloud services and large-scale data.

Key job responsibilities

Build services that check purchase requests and orders against finance rules in near real time, then correct or flag issues before approval.
Automate financial controls, such as reviews of fixed assets, leases, cost centers, open orders, so finance teams spend less time collecting data by hand and more time acting on exceptions.
Build data pipelines on AWS, including Lambda, StepFunctions, Glue, EMR, DDB, and S3, that feed C-Hub/dashboards finance teams use during month-end close and audit reviews.
Build AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with the Strands SDK, including MCP tools, context and memory management, evaluation, harnesses, and guardrails that keep finance answers accurate.
Big data experience with Spark, StarRocks, or similar OLAP engines.
Build web applications and browser extensions in React and TypeScript that let finance users review exceptions, filter large datasets, and export results.
Turn defined business requirements into technical designs, review them with senior engineers, and take them from prototype to production.
Own your services in production. Write the tests, alarms, and automated rollbacks that let a change reach customers in hours, not days. Take part in on-call rotation.
Work directly with finance, accounting, product, and data science partners, and explain technical tradeoffs.

A day in the life

Most of your day goes to building. You might start by looking into an alarm from an overnight data job that feeds a finance control. Then you meet an accounting partner to design how a manual review could run automatically. After lunch, you write code and tests and ship the change through an automated pipeline the same day. Some weeks, you test a new AI model against an evaluation set to see if it gives better answers. Near month-end close, you answer finance users who want to know why a control flagged a transaction.

About The Team

We are a team of software engineers who build the tools that keep Amazon's spending accurate and its financial reports audit-ready. Our customers are finance analysts, accountants, and employees across Amazon who buy goods and services. We own our products end to end, from data pipelines and services to the web apps and AI agents people use every day. We ship changes through automated pipelines and measure our work by the manual effort and errors we remove. We value clear writing, careful reviews, and engineers who ask why a process exists before they automate it.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
Experience programming with at least one software programming language
Bachelor's degree or equivalent

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
Knowledge of machine learning model architecture and inference
Knowledge of computer architecture, operating systems, and parallel computing
Knowledge of professional software engineering & best practices for full software development life cycle, including coding standards, software architectures, code reviews, source control management, continuous deployments, testing, and operational excellence

Hybrid work environment - 3 days/week onsite

Robust benefits package, including:

Employee Business Networks

added.description:
Globality is the autonomous sourcing platform to manage the entire intake to award process.

At Globality, we build agentic technology that transforms how global enterprises source goods and services — autonomously, at scale, and without the inefficiencies that have defined procurement for decades. Our platform interprets purchase intent, generates sourcing materials, evaluates suppliers, and executes negotiation strategies without manual intervention.

The Role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to build the agentic platform at the core of Glo. You will own features end to end across the stack: the React and TypeScript interfaces where procurement teams direct and review agents, the services and APIs behind them, and the orchestration layer where agents plan, call tools, and take action.

You will build with agentic coding as your default way of working. Coding agents help you plan, implement, test, and review, and you apply the judgment that turns their output into reliable production software. You will work closely with product and design, and you will have real influence over architecture and over how our team builds with agents.

What You Will Do

Design, build, and ship full stack features for an agentic sourcing platform, from React and TypeScript interfaces to backend services, data models, and APIs
Build agent orchestration: planning and tool-calling loops, multi-agent workflows, long-running tasks, retries, and human approval checkpoints
Create interfaces for human-agent collaboration, including streaming output, live progress, reasoning and evidence views, confidence indicators, and controls to pause, redirect, or override an agent
Develop with coding agents (such as Claude Code, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot) as your primary workflow, running tasks in parallel, directing and reviewing their work, and holding the result to production standards
Build the context, conventions, and guardrails that make coding agents effective in our codebase, including project instructions, reusable skills, test harnesses, and review checklists
Integrate LLMs and external tools through APIs and protocols such as the Model Context Protocol, and manage prompts, context, cost, and latency as part of the application design
Build evaluation, tracing, and observability for agent behavior, so the team can measure quality, replay runs, and improve results with evidence
Design for security, privacy, and auditability in line with SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001:2022, GDPR, and CCPA requirements, including permissions, data boundaries, and logging for autonomous actions
Write unit, integration, and end-to-end tests, and review code for reliability, security, and maintainability, including code written by agents
Own services in production, including deployment, monitoring, and performance tuning for real-time, data-intensive workloads
Take part in sprint planning, architecture discussions, and technical direction alongside senior engineers

What You Bring

5+ years of professional software engineering experience across the stack
Hands-on experience shipping production software with agentic coding tools, including delegating multi-step tasks, running agents in parallel, and reviewing and correcting their output
A clear point of view on working with coding agents: how you structure context and instructions, scope tasks, verify results, and decide when to take the keyboard yourself
Experience building LLM-powered or agentic features in production, such as tool calling, retrieval, structured outputs, streaming, or multi-step workflows
Solid backend fundamentals: API design (REST or GraphQL), relational data modeling, queues and background jobs, and asynchronous and event-driven patterns
Experience with real-time delivery of data to the browser over WebSockets or server-sent events, including partial, streaming, and failure states
Working knowledge of cloud infrastructure, containers, and CI/CD, and the discipline to own what you ship in production
Strong testing and code review habits that hold up when much of the first draft comes from an agent
Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical tradeoffs to non-engineering stakeholders

Why Globality

The opportunity is enormous.
Enterprise procurement is one of the last major business functions to be transformed by AI. We're not optimizing at the margins — we're fundamentally rethinking how trillions of dollars get spent.

The team is world-class.
Our leadership team brings decades of experience from leading global enterprises, and our culture is built for people who want real ownership, not titles.

You'll have real impact.
This isn't a role where you execute someone else's playbook. You'll shape the strategy, build the programs, and see the direct business impact of your work.

We work together — literally.
We're in-office 4 days a week in Palo Alto because the best ideas – and the fastest decisions – happen face to face. One day is yours to work wherever you’re most effective.

The anticipated annual base salary range for this position is $150,000 - $250,000. Actual compensation may vary based on factors such as experience, skills, and location. added.description:
About Rocket Lab

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SOFTWARE ENGINEER I - ROBOTICS

Based onsite at Rocket Lab Robotics in Pasadena, CA, the Software Engineer I - Robotics will develop software for robotic platforms, motion-control systems, sensing systems, machine interfaces, test systems, and production support tools. This role is hands-on and works closely with mechanical, electrical, controls, manufacturing, test, quality, and operations teams to turn robotics concepts into reliable working systems.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on software engineer with strong robotics or hardware-integrated software experience, sound software engineering fundamentals, and the ability to develop reliable software in a fast-paced hardware development environment. You will support design, implementation, simulation, hardware bring-up, integration, test, deployment, troubleshooting, and production support for robotic systems.

What You'll Get To Do

Develop and maintain software for robotic systems, embedded interfaces, control applications, test systems, and operator-facing tools.
Implement software for robotic platforms, motion-control systems, sensing systems, machine interfaces, production support tools, and hardware test environments.
Support software development from concept through implementation, simulation, hardware bring-up, integration, test, deployment, troubleshooting, and production support.
Partner with mechanical, electrical, controls, systems, manufacturing, test, and quality teams to define requirements, interfaces, verification approaches, and release criteria.
Integrate software with motors, actuators, encoders, sensors, motion controllers, embedded systems, machine vision systems, industrial networks, and robotic equipment.
Troubleshoot issues across software, controls, electrical hardware, sensors, actuators, networks, robotic hardware, and production equipment.
Support software quality through code reviews, version control, CI/CD, automated testing, documentation, release practices, and production support practices.
Communicate software status, technical risks, trade studies, test results, and implementation plans to technical and cross-functional stakeholders.

You'll Bring These Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics, or Aerospace Engineering
Strong proficiency in C++ and/or Python.
Experience with robotics frameworks such as ROS or ROS 2, including real-time variants or real-time robotics applications.
Hands-on experience integrating software with hardware such as motors, actuators, encoders, sensors, motion controllers, embedded systems, machine vision, or industrial networks.
Experience with real-time or embedded software, including an understanding of control loops, deterministic timing, and hardware bring-up.
Solid software engineering fundamentals, including architecture, Git-based workflows, code reviews, CI/CD, automated testing, release practices, documentation, and production support.
Experience developing in Linux environments.
Demonstrated ability to define requirements, evaluate alternatives, support stakeholder alignment, and deliver software solutions in a cross-functional hardware development environment.
U.S Citizenship due to program requirements

These Qualifications Would Be Nice To Have

Experience with motion planning, kinematics and dynamics, trajectory generation, controls software, robot calibration, perception systems, state estimation, or sensor fusion.
Experience with real-time operating systems, bare-metal embedded development, hard real-time control, or safety-critical software.
Experience with spacecraft, embedded, or industrial communication interfaces such as CAN/CANopen, SpaceWire, MIL-STD-1553, EtherCAT, SPI/I2C, Ethernet, TCP/IP, Modbus, OPC UA, PLCs, safety controllers, or other fieldbus protocols.
Experience with simulation, digital twins, hardware-in-the-loop, software-in-the-loop, flatsat, testbed environments, automated test equipment, or production test systems.
Experience designing for fault tolerance, redundancy, cybersecurity, configuration control, or operation in radiation, thermal, vacuum, or other harsh environments.
Experience working in aerospace, defense, space, advanced manufacturing, industrial robotics, medical device, or other high-reliability hardware environments.
Strong communication skills and the ability to translate complex technical issues into clear plans, risks, and decisions for technical and non-technical stakeholders.

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. Spacecraft represent the most pressing unmet need across the entire aerospace industry. As more launch vehicles come online and the cost to orbit decreases, more companies launching payloads to space continue to emerge.

For the first time in history, this influx of payload companies combined with reduced launch costs has resulted in a massive increase in need for commercial spacecraft platforms, known as satellite buses. These buses hold the payloads of our customers and are flown on launch vehicles.

Apex manufactures these satellite buses at scale using a combination of software, vertical integration, and hardware that is designed for manufacturing. Our spacecraft enable the future of society: ranging from earth observation to communications and more.

We’d love for you to join us on our mission of providing humankind access to the galaxy beyond our planet.

About The Role

As an Operating Systems Engineer on Apex's Flight Software team, you will design, develop,
and own
the software that brings our spacecraft to life. You will tackle the hardest problems in autonomous systems and build robust software that enables reliable spacecraft operation 24/7, across every phase of a mission. You will work closely with our mission operations, GNC, and hardware teams to architect new systems, prototype ideas, and turn them into mission-critical software that ultimately flies.

Experience in the space industry is not necessary to thrive at Apex. Instead, we are looking for motivated engineers who enjoy solving complex problems, balance technical rigor with practicality, and thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.

The Flight Software team is composed of three interconnected teams: high-level application software, operating system software, and embedded software.
There is significant collaboration and crossover across these teams.

Responsibilities

Design, develop, and own mission-critical software for satellite systems throughout the full software lifecycle, from initial architecture and development through deployment and operations.
Develop, configure, and maintain embedded Linux platforms and bootloader frameworks, including Yocto, Buildroot, WolfBoot, and U-Boot.
Design, implement, and validate firmware update mechanisms, including bootloader integration, secure firmware deployment, and recovery procedures.
Design and implement security enhancements across complex software architectures to improve system integrity, resilience, and secure operation.

U.S. Person status is required as this position needs to access export controlled data.
Bachelor's degree in CS, EE or equivalent, or equivalent professional experience.
2+ years writing code for operating systems, ideally Yocto or embedded Linux on spacecraft, robotics, automotive, or other hardware what that interacts with the physical world
Strong proficiency in programming languages such as Python, C++, or Rust

Preferred Requirements

1+ year of flight software experience
Experience developing, testing, deploying, and troubleshooting mission-critical satellite software from prototyping through flight operations.
Experience with embedded Linux platforms and bootloader frameworks (e.g., Yocto, Buildroot, WolfBoot, U-Boot).
Experience bringing up new avionics and flight hardware from initial power-on through functional verification.
Experience with hardware/software integration, schematic analysis, and hardware debugging using oscilloscopes and logic analyzers.
Familiarity with spacecraft attitude control systems, including reaction wheels, magnetorquers, thrusters, and associated sensors.
Experience designing, implementing, and validating firmware update mechanisms, including bootloader integration, secure firmware deployment, and update recovery.
Experience designing secure systems and implementing security enhancements in complex software architectures.

Why Join Apex?

Apex believes in creating a work environment that you look forward to embracing every day. Our employees love working at Apex, and we want you to love it too. We're a fast-growing startup that has raised more than $500M in funding, and we invest heavily in our people from day one.

added.title: Software Engineer, Sentry Software (Manufacturing)
added.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

The Sentry Tower Software team is responsible for developing robotic systems that provide force protection capabilities, monitoring the perimeter of secure areas, land or sea, for approaching people, vehicles, and vessels. We live in a world where security officers are increasingly overwhelmed by sensor data feeds. Our products leverage advanced sensor fusion and autonomy to seamlessly render activity in the environment to Lattice's common operating picture.

About The Job

We are looking for a Software Engineer with a focus in Manufacturing to join our rapidly growing team in Costa Mesa. In this role you will be responsible for building and maintaining software for current and next generation Sentry Tower systems. You will be responsible for developing automated test suites and user-friendly interfaces to streamline hardware verification and issue diagnosis for non-technical users. You will implement robust error-capturing mechanisms that provide actionable insights for efficient troubleshooting and quality assurance.

Every tower we ship passes through this software. It is what proves a unit works before it leaves the floor, which makes it the last chance to catch a defect while the hardware is still in reach and the fix costs an hour instead of a trip to a site. A test that passes when it should not have is the most expensive kind of bug we have, because it ships.

The honest version: your users are technicians on a production floor, not engineers, and their time is the constraint. That means a lot of the work is unglamorous by design: clear error messages, tooling that fails in an obvious way, and diagnostics a person can follow at 6am without calling you. You will also be pulled into whatever is blocking the line, which does not wait for your sprint. The upside is a feedback loop most software engineers never get, since the people using what you built are in the same building and will tell you within a day.

Our Product: https://www.anduril.com/hardware/sentry/

What You'll Do

Develop automated test suites to verify hardware functionality and performance.
Create user-friendly interfaces to facilitate issue diagnosis for non-technical users.
Implement robust error-capturing mechanisms to provide actionable insights.
Collaborate with hardware and quality assurance teams to ensure seamless integration of testing tools.
Work directly with the technicians and manufacturing engineers who use your tooling every shift, and treat their time as the thing you are optimizing.
Continuously improve testing frameworks to enhance efficiency and reliability.

Required Qualifications

Experience building test automation, instrumentation, or tooling for hardware, and comfort working on a bench with the hardware in front of you.
Proficiency in Python for test and tooling work, plus 2+ years in Rust or C++ to work in the services under test.
Solid grasp of networking principles, including CAN and Ethernet protocols, along with expertise in hardware interfacing, diagnostic tools (e.g., Wireshark, CANoe), and cybersecurity principles as they pertain to secure and reliable sensor data transmission.
Strong engineering background from industry or school, ideally in areas/fields such as Computer Science, Software Engineering, Mathematics, or Physics.
US person status required, with eligibility to obtain and maintain a US security clearance.

US Salary Range

$220,000—$292,000 USD

Benefits

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind

Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

About The Job

Sentry Towers protect perimeters for allied partner nations as well as US customers, and those deployments are their own engineering problem. A partner program brings its own site conditions, its own communications and network environment, its own integration requirements, and its own operators, and none of it is solved by shipping the standard configuration and hoping. We're hiring a Software Engineer dedicated to one such program: making our towers work for that customer, in their environment, and keeping them working. This is a customer with no second system to fall back on. When a tower is down, the perimeter it was watching is being watched by people instead, and the fix depends on an engineer who understands both our software and their site.

This is a hands-on integration and support role rather than a pure feature-development one. You will own the software configuration for this program's towers, built on our declarative NixOS platform: product configuration, network integration into the customer's environment, payload and sensor setup, and the deployment and update path for systems in the customer's hands. When something doesn't work in the field, you're the engineer who reproduces it, root-causes it, and either fixes it or drives the fix with the team that owns the component.

Expect meaningful travel, roughly 30% of your time, much of it extended international trips for installation, integration, and operator support. Some of it is not optional: when a program milestone depends on being on site, you'll be on site. The compensation for that is direct contact with the people using what you build. You will watch an operator use your work, learn things no bug report would have told you, and carry them back.

Worth weighing honestly before you apply. This is reactive work by nature: your week can get reorganized by what broke, and the roadmap you planned on Monday is not always the one you follow. You will go deep on one program rather than broad across the product, which builds unusually specific expertise and means your work is harder to point at than a shipped feature. Time zones will cost you: some of the coordination happens early, some late, and it is not evenly distributed. People take this role and love it, and people take it and find out they wanted to be writing features. Both are worth knowing about yourself first.

Our Product: https://www.anduril.com/sentry

What You'll Do

Own the software configuration for this program's tower variants in our declarative platform, from product definitions through payload and sensor configuration to image builds.
Integrate towers into the customer's network and communications environment, covering addressing, routing, backhaul, and any interfaces the program requires.
Own the deployment and software update path for the program's fielded systems, including provisioning, staged rollout, and verification that an update landed cleanly.
Travel to customer sites for installation, integration, commissioning, and operator support, including extended international deployments, at approximately 30% of your time.
Be the program's technical front line: triage field issues, reproduce them on a bench or in simulation, root-cause them, and either fix them directly or drive the fix with the owning team.
Build the tooling, documentation, and runbooks that let field personnel and the customer's own operators resolve routine problems without escalating.
Represent the program back into engineering, making sure customer requirements and field realities reach the teams whose roadmaps need to reflect them.

2+ years of professional software engineering, with time spent on systems that are deployed and operated rather than only developed.
Solid Linux systems skills: the command line, systemd, log analysis, and the ability to diagnose a misbehaving service on a machine you didn't set up.
Practical networking competence: addressing and subnetting, routing, DNS, VLANs, and packet capture, enough to integrate a system into someone else's network and debug it when it doesn't come up.
Proficiency in at least one of Python, Rust, C++, or Go, and willingness to work in Rust and C++ where our services live.
Willingness and ability to travel approximately 30% of the time, including extended international trips that cannot be rescheduled around, and to work effectively on customer sites.
Strong written communication and follow-through, since much of this role is coordinating across time zones and leaving behind documentation someone else depends on.
US person status required. Active US Secret clearance, or a previously granted Secret clearance eligible for reactivation.

Experience with declarative configuration management or infrastructure-as-code. Nix or NixOS is what we use; adjacent tooling is a fine starting point.
Field service, field engineering, or deployment engineering background, especially on hardware systems.
Experience integrating with radios, satellite terminals, cellular backhaul, or constrained and intermittent network links.
Prior work supporting international or defense customers, or in a program-facing engineering role.
Additional language skills, or experience working with non-native-English-speaking operators and partner engineering teams.
